findings.message: reads sensitive environment variables and makes network requests (potential secret exfiltration)
findings.remediation: Never read sensitive environment variables and transmit them over the network.
findings.impact: Environment variables often contain API keys, tokens, and database credentials.
findings.attack_vector: process.env.SECRET accessed in plugin code — if combined with network calls, secrets are exfiltrated.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and use a fixed allowlisted command with bounded arguments.
findings.downgrade: Downgraded from high: no system-impact pattern matched.
findings.impact: Attackers can execute arbitrary OS commands on the host, leading to full system compromise.
findings.attack_vector: Plugin spawns a child process with attacker-controlled arguments; no user approval gate.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: reads a likely secret source and opens a network connection in the same source file
findings.remediation: Keep secrets out of agent-visible output and require an allowlisted destination before egress.
findings.impact: Secret source + network sink in same file = direct exfiltration pathway for credentials.
findings.attack_vector: File reads secrets (process.env/credential files) AND opens network connections — data flows out.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: reads environment secrets and makes network requests in the same file
findings.remediation: Separate secret handling from network requests; never combine in the same code flow.
findings.impact: Environment secrets combined with network requests create a direct exfiltration channel.
findings.attack_vector: process.env.* + fetch/http.request in same file — secrets flow to external endpoints.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
